land.text: the eastern half "still ruled from Ötüken": the Mongolian Plateau and the southern steppe

predecessors.note: Eastern Turkic Khaganate page infobox: 'Göktürk civil war, Eastern Khaganate founded: 581', 'Administrative division of the First Turkic Khaganate (581-603)', 'Independent khaganate (603-630)'. Cliopatria's Eastern row begins in 587; the dossier keeps 587.

land.text: the Ordos Loop, where "Taizong made the Ashina live"

successors.note: 'Reconquest by Tang dynasty: 645' (infobox 'Buffer state of the Tang dynasty (639-645)'); the Ashina buffer between the Yellow River and the Gobi falls to the Tang.
'After the fall of the Khaganate Zhenzhu Khan (629-645) of the Xueyantuo ruled much of the north'. The Xueyantuo have no Cliopatria row and no dossier yet.

Infobox 'Succeeded by: ... Second Turkic Khaganate'; 'Turkic power was restored by the Second Turkic Khaganate (682-744)' (Second Turkic Khaganate page: Ilterish Qaghan, Ötüken). No Cliopatria row carries it under that name; the brief flags a probable label swap of Türgesh 692-749 and Turks 666-756.

capitals.name: Ötüken (Orkhon valley, Mongolia)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Ötüken' (one capital listed). The Ötüken site is the Orkhon valley near modern Kharkhorin (Second Turkic Khaganate page: 'centered on Ötüken in the upper reaches of the Orkhon River'); the point is approximate. After 630 the pages give the Ashina no seat.

capitals.name: Dingxiang (Hohhot area, Inner Mongolia)
capitals.note: Ashina Simo page: in spring 641, after crossing the Yellow River, Simo (Qilibi Khan) 'established his headquarters at Dingxiang (in modern Hohhot, Inner Mongolia)'; in winter 641 he withdrew 'within the Great Wall to Shuo Prefecture' after a Xueyantuo attack. No seat is named for 631-640 or for 642-645; the point is the Hohhot gazetteer position, approximate for the ancient Dingxiang.

rulers.name: Tardu (Western Qaghan)
rulers.title: Western khagan, briefly reunifying the empire
rulers.note: Eastern Turkic Khaganate page: Tardu "briefly reunified the Turkic empire (599-603)"; the Sui "poisoned the wells forcing him to retreat".

rulers.name: Illig Qaghan
rulers.note: The last independent ruler; captured in 630.

rulers.name: Qilibi Khan
rulers.title: khan of the Tang buffer state
rulers.note: Installed by Taizong on 13 August 639 (Göktürks page).

keyframe_review.note: 2.65 M km2 for 587-611 against the infobox 4.0 M km2 for 624 (the Cliopatria 623 shape is 2.68 M km2, ratio 0.67, within the factor of two; the shape is the smaller, so it may lack the Altai and Dzungarian edge). The pages give no territory for the eastern half beyond the Mongolian Plateau, 'still ruled from Ötüken', and no east-west border (the Western Turkic Khaganate page states no east-west border).

2.68 M km2 for 612-616: Cliopatria adds 145 cells (Gansu 66, Hexi Corridor 12, Inner Mongolia 79). No page opened dates it; Shibi Qaghan (609-619) besieged Emperor Yang at Yanmen in 615 without a border change. Unverified: page budget. Shibi Khagan page, opened for this cell change: no land is named for 609-614; the only dated gain is the autumn 615 attack on the Yanmen region (and a Wuyuan county commander who 'submitted to Shibi Qaghan in 618'); still unverified.

2.78 M km2 for 617-622: Cliopatria adds the Ordos and the Hetao (457 cells, all inside its Sui 616 shape and none inside the Sui 617 shape). Eastern Turkic page: Yami 'had the Han people build him a house in the Ordos country' (undated); 'In 617, when tens of thousands of Turks reached Taiyuan, they found the gates open'. The pages opened do not explain the addition (unverified: page budget; ledger 617 at confidence 1).

2.68 M km2 for 623-625: the Ordos and Hetao leave again (457 cells, into no Cliopatria polity; the Tang 623 shape holds 8). The Göktürks page has the Turks backing the rebel Liu Heita against the Tang in 622-623; no page opened explains the loss (ledger 623, confidence 1; unverified: page budget).

2.71 M km2 for the single year 626; the shape reaches 34.4 N (Gansu 77, Ningxia 48, Guanzhong 22 cells, 43 within 200 km of Chang'an). First Turkic Khaganate page: 'Illig Qaghan at the Wei River (September 23, 626)'; Eastern Turkic page: 'In 626, he reached the gates of Chang'an'. A raid, drawn as contested in the ledger.
2.68 M km2 for 627: the 623 shape again; the Wei River cells are given back (ledger 627; no page opened dates a treaty).

2.68 M km2 for 628-629. 'In 627-629, an unusual cold led to mass livestock deaths and famine. The Xueyantuo, Uyghurs, Bayegu and some of Illig's people rebelled and in 629 were joined by the Khitans and Taizong.' The shape is still whole although the rebels' lands (the Xueyantuo from 629) are no longer Illig's by the page; kept, the northern steppe goes in 630 by the ledger.

correction.text: the Ordos Loop, where "Taizong made the Ashina live"

keyframe_review.note: 2.51 M km2 for 630-632: Cliopatria takes the Hetao, Ordos, Inner Mongolia and Gansu strip (794 cells, all inside its Tang 630 shape) and leaves the northern steppe to the Eastern Göktürks until its Tang shape swallows it in 633 (10,547 of the 10,553 cells). Eastern Turkic page: 'Six Tang armies attacked on a 1,200 km front', 'Illig was captured in 630'; afterwards 'Zhenzhu Khan (629-645) of the Xueyantuo ruled much of the north' and 'Taizong made the Ashina live inside the Ordos Loop'. The northern steppe is therefore the Xueyantuo's; the Turks' own land is the settlement in the Ordos Loop (a Tang vassal 630-639, buffer state 639-645 by the infobox). Reviewer fix applied: the gain of the Ordos from the Tang is ledger 630, and ledger 630 (Tang loss) no longer includes these cells.

correction.text: the Ordos Loop, where "Taizong made the Ashina live"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 633-638: Cliopatria has no Eastern Göktürk shape after 632 (its Tang shape holds the whole steppe). Taizong 'made the Ashina live inside the Ordos Loop'; the Second Turkic Khaganate page: the surrendered tribes were organised into 'six prefectures under four area commands' in the Ordos Loop. Drawn as the Ashina settlement; the Tang dossier carries the suzerainty (vassal tint).

correction.text: the land "between the Yellow River and Gobi"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 639-641: 'In 639, after Ashina Jiesheshuai attempted to assassinate Emperor Taizong, Taizong made them live between the Yellow River and Gobi'; Qilibi Khan ruled the buffer state 639-643 (the Göktürks page: installed on 13 August 639; Jiesheshuai's attack 19 May 639). The Hetao is the land north of the river's bend. The Ordos beyond the Hetao leaves in 639 (ledger 639 loss).

correction.text: the Ordos Loop, where "Taizong made the Ashina live"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 642-645: 'In 642, the Xueyantuo drove them south of the river', back to the Ordos; 'Reconquest by Tang dynasty: 645' (infobox). Chebi Khan's revival of 646-650 'was captured by the Chinese and Uyghurs'. The Ordos beyond the Hetao returns in 642 (ledger 642 gain) and the Hetao beyond the Ordos is lost (ledger 642 loss).

region.text: the Mongolian Plateau and the southern steppe, ruled from Ötüken

ledger.note: 587: Bagha succeeds in the east. 'In 587 both Apa and Ishbara died during the Göktürk civil war'; Bagha Qaghan (587-588) then Tulan. Infobox 'Göktürk civil war, Eastern Khaganate founded: 581'; the realm formally divided in 603. Cliopatria draws the Eastern Göktürks from 587 on the Mongolian Plateau, 'still ruled from Ötüken' (First Turkic Khaganate page).

region.text: the Ordos and the Hetao: the 457 cells that the 617 shape adds to the 612 shape

ledger.note: 617: the Turks hold the Ordos and Hetao. Cliopatria adds 457 cells inside its Sui 616 shape in 617; the page has Yami with 'a house in the Ordos country' (undated) and Turks at Taiyuan in 617 ('they found the gates open'). The pages opened do not say who held the Ordos before; the year and the land are Cliopatria's (confidence 1). Liang Shidu page: Liang Shidu, based at Xia Province (modern Yulin) later Shuofang, 'submitted to Shibi Khan' in the 610s, was named 'Dadupiqie Qaghan' and, with Turkic help, 'occupied the Ordos Desert' (no years), and declared himself Emperor of Liang in 617; so the 617 land is probably his regime under Turkic protection rather than Turkic territory proper (a possible vassal relation 617-628, counterpart liang-shidu; not recorded because the Cliopatria shape, not a page, dates the cells).

region.text: the Ordos and the Hetao: the 457 cells that the 617 shape adds to the 612 shape

ledger.note: 623: the Ordos and Hetao leave the Turkic shape. Cliopatria removes the 457 cells in 623 and gives them to no polity (the Tang 623 shape holds 8); no page opened explains it. (confidence 1). Liang Shidu page: Turkic forces were at Shuofang in 622 and attacked Lin and Kuang Prefectures (Yulin) in summer 623, and Liang's regime fell on 28 May or 3 June 628 (his cousin Liang Luoren surrendered Shuofang to the Tang), so the Ordos was not empty or 'nobody's' in 623-628: the 623 removal is Cliopatria's, not the page's.

region.text: Gansu, Ningxia and the Guanzhong up to the Wei River near Chang'an: the 148 cells that the 626 shape adds

ledger.note: 626: Illig Qaghan reaches the Wei River. 'Illig Qaghan at the Wei River (September 23, 626)'; Eastern Turkic page: 'In 626, he reached the gates of Chang'an'.

region.text: Gansu, Ningxia and the Guanzhong up to the Wei River near Chang'an: the 148 cells that the 626 shape adds

ledger.note: 627: the Turks withdraw from the Guanzhong. Cliopatria gives the 148 cells back in 627; the pages opened date no treaty. Liang Shidu page: in 626 Illig and Ashina Shibobi 'attacked Chang'an and withdrew after Emperor Taizong met them with added tribute' (the Wei River agreement of 626); 627 is the year of Cliopatria's shape change.

region.text: the southern steppe and the Tang frontier strip: the Hetao, Ordos, Inner Mongolia and Gansu cells that the 628 shape holds and the 630 shape lacks

ledger.note: 629: Tang armies attack. 'Six Tang armies attacked on a 1,200 km front' after the Xueyantuo, Uyghurs and Bayegu had rebelled (627-629) and the Khitans joined in 629. [Reviewer ia-01-c: confidence 3 -> 2; the Eastern Turkic Khaganate page names no land for the 629-630 campaign (only 'a 1,200 km front'); the region is Cliopatria's.]

region.text: the southern steppe and the Tang frontier strip: the Hetao, Ordos, Inner Mongolia and Gansu cells that the 628 shape holds and the 630 shape lacks

ledger.note: 630: Illig Qaghan is captured. 'Illig was captured in 630'; infobox 'Conquest by Tang dynasty: 630'; the First Turkic page has Li Jing defeat the Eastern Turks at Yinshan on 27 March 630. [Reviewer ia-01-c: confidence 3 -> 2; the Eastern Turkic Khaganate page names no land for the 629-630 campaign (only 'a 1,200 km front'); the region is Cliopatria's.]

region.text: the southern steppe and the Tang frontier strip, without the Ordos Loop: the Hetao, Inner Mongolia and Gansu cells that the 628 shape holds and the 630 shape lacks, less the 136 Ordos cells that the Ashina keep (ledger 630 gain)

ledger.note: 630: the southern steppe and the frontier strip pass to the Tang. 794 cells of Cliopatria's 628 shape lie inside the Tang 630 shape (658 once the 136 Ordos cells are taken out, see the gain below); 'Taizong made the Ashina live inside the Ordos Loop'. [Reviewer ia-01-c: confidence 3 -> 2; the Eastern Turkic Khaganate page names no land for the 629-630 campaign (only 'a 1,200 km front'); the region is Cliopatria's.] Reviewer fix applied: the region no longer includes the Ordos cells that the 630 keyframe keeps.

minus.text: the Ordos Loop, where "Taizong made the Ashina live"

region.text: the rest of the 630 shape: the northern steppe of Outer Mongolia, "much of the north" ruled by the Xueyantuo

ledger.note: 630: the northern steppe passes to the Xueyantuo. 'After the fall of the Khaganate Zhenzhu Khan (629-645) of the Xueyantuo ruled much of the north'. Cliopatria keeps this land in the Eastern shape to 632 and in the Tang shape from 633; the pages put it with the Xueyantuo.

region.text: the Ordos Loop, where "Taizong made the Ashina live"

ledger.note: 630: the Ashina are settled in the Ordos Loop. Eastern Turkic page: infobox 'Vassal khaganate of the Tang dynasty (630-639)', and after the defeat of Illig Qaghan in 630 'Taizong made the Ashina live inside the Ordos Loop' (the sentence itself is undated); Second Turkic Khaganate page: 'After the Tang dynasty defeated the Eastern Turkic Khaganate in 630' the surrendered Turks were organised 'into six prefectures under four area commands' in the Ordos Loop (no year for the resettlement). The year is the pages' link to the defeat, the land is the researcher's reading of 'Ordos Loop' (confidence 2). The Ordos lies inside Cliopatria's Tang 630 shape (884 of 884 cells), so the land is a Tang loss; the Tang worked example carries the Ashina only as a vassal tint (vassal_start 630, vassal_end 645, counterpart eastern-gokturks): ea-04 must not draw the Ordos as direct Tang land in 630-645. Reviewer fix applied: keyframe 630 had no gain behind it.

region.text: the land "between the Yellow River and Gobi" beyond the Ordos Loop: the 166 Hetao cells outside the Ordos

ledger.note: 639: the Ashina are settled north of the Yellow River. 'Taizong made them live between the Yellow River and Gobi' after the assassination attempt of 19 May 639 (Göktürks page); Qilibi Khan installed on 13 August 639. A Tang assignment: the Tang dossier carries the suzerainty. Reviewer fix applied: the Hetao cells inside the Ordos (205) were already held, so the gain is Hetao minus Ordos; the Ordos beyond the Hetao is given up below.

region.text: the Ordos Loop outside the Hetao: the 679 cells the Ashina leave when they move north of the river

ledger.note: 639: the Ashina leave the Ordos Loop. 'In 639, after Ashina Jiesheshuai attempted to assassinate Emperor Taizong, Taizong made them live between the Yellow River and Gobi'; the Ashina Simo page: on 13 August 639 the Turks were ordered to follow him north of the Yellow River 'to settle between the Great Wall and the Gobi Desert'. The 679 Ordos cells outside the Hetao return to the Tang; the 205 Hetao cells inside the Ordos stay with the Ashina. Reviewer fix applied: keyframe 639 dropped these cells with no event.

region.text: the land "between the Yellow River and Gobi" north of the Ordos Loop: the 166 Hetao cells outside the Ordos

ledger.note: 642: the Xueyantuo drive the Ashina south of the Yellow River. 'In 642, the Xueyantuo drove them south of the river.' Reviewer fix applied: the 205 Hetao cells inside the Ordos stay with the Ashina (they are in the 642 keyframe), so the loss is Hetao minus Ordos. The Ashina Simo page has the Turks, after a Xueyantuo attack in winter 641, withdraw 'within the Great Wall to Shuo Prefecture' (the Eastern Turkic page dates the retreat 642).

region.text: the Ordos Loop outside the Hetao: the 679 cells the Ashina return to

ledger.note: 642: the Ashina fall back into the Ordos Loop. 'In 642 the Xueyantuo drove them south of the river.' The Ordos cells outside the Hetao are Tang land again held by the Ashina under Tang protection (the Ashina Simo page has them, around the new year 645, ask to settle in Sheng and Xia (Yulin) Prefectures). Reviewer fix applied: keyframe 642 added these cells with no event. The Tang dossier must treat 639-645 as in the 630 gain above (vassal tint, not direct Tang land).

region.text: the Ordos Loop, where "Taizong made the Ashina live"

ledger.note: 645: the Tang reconquer the buffer state. Infobox 'Reconquest by Tang dynasty: 645'; Duomi Khan of the Xueyantuo then 'planned to attack China' (645-646). Chebi's revival (646-650) failed; the Second Turkic Khaganate restored Turkic power in 682.

wars.name: Siege of Yanmen
wars.outcome: Shibi Qaghan besieged Emperor Yang of Sui at Yanmen in Shanxi on 11 September 615 (First Turkic Khaganate page) with 100,000 cavalry (Göktürks page); no border changed.
wars.note: Eastern Turkic page: in 615 the Sui lured Shibi's Sogdian advisor into a trap and killed him; the same year Emperor Yang assigned Li Yuan against the Turks.

wars.name: Turkic raid on the Wei River

zones.text: Gansu, Ningxia and the Guanzhong up to the Wei River near Chang'an: the 148 cells that the 626 shape adds

wars.outcome: Illig Qaghan reached the Wei River at Chang'an on 23 September 626 and withdrew; the Cliopatria shape of 626 holds the Wei River country for a year.

wars.name: Revolt of the Xueyantuo, Uyghurs and Khitans
wars.outcome: Famine from an unusual cold in 627-629 led the Xueyantuo, Uyghurs, Bayegu and part of Illig's people to rebel, joined by the Khitans and Taizong in 629; Zhenzhu Khan of the Xueyantuo ruled 'much of the north' from 629.

wars.name: Tang campaign against the Eastern Turks

zones.text: the Ordos and the steppe south of the Gobi

wars.outcome: Tang victory: six armies on a 1,200 km front, Illig captured in 630; the surrendered Turks settled in the Ordos Loop.
wars.note: The First Turkic page gives the decisive battle as Yinshan, 27 March 630, under Li Jing.

wars.name: Xueyantuo-Ashina war

zones.text: the land "between the Yellow River and Gobi"

wars.outcome: The Xueyantuo drove the Ashina south of the Yellow River in 642.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; the pages date no treaty line. The Tang frontier from 630 is approximate, and the settlement strips of 633-645 follow named landscapes (Ordos Loop, between the Yellow River and the Gobi), not surveyed lines.

notes: Cliopatria row Eastern Göktürks 587..632 (8 shapes). The eastern and western rows share Wikidata Q205466 (Göktürks) but they are two states: the Western Turkic Khaganate page has the Western khaganate 'an administrative region of the First Turkic Khaganate (581-603)' and an 'independent empire (603-657)', and says 'Within 35 years the Western Turkic Khaganate and the Eastern Turkic Khaganate were independent polities'; Tardu's brief reunification of 599-603 is the only joint rule. Start: Cliopatria's 587 is kept (infobox 581, independence 603). End: moved to 645 from Cliopatria's 632, so that the Tang vassal and buffer relations (the Tang dossier's vassal events 630-645) have a state to attach to; the Cliopatria 630-632 shape is replaced by the Ordos strip because the northern steppe is the Xueyantuo's, and new keyframes 633, 639 and 642 follow the pages. Unverified: the +145 cells of 612 (Shibi Khagan page names no land for 609-614) and the Cliopatria removal of the Ordos and Hetao in 623, which the Liang Shidu page contradicts (Liang Shidu's regime at Shuofang under Turkic protection to 628); the 617-622 cells are probably that regime, a possible vassal relation with counterpart liang-shidu. The Sui suzerainty of 603-609 ('as a sort of Sui vassal'; Göktürks page: 'declared allegiance to the Sui dynasty', undated) belongs to the Sui dossier (vassal event with counterpart eastern-gokturks); the Tang vassal and buffer status of 630-645 to the Tang dossier. The Kyrgyz vassalage is recorded in gokturk-khaganate (553-586) and not repeated: the page says only that Muqan 'controlled the Yenisei Kyrgyz', and the Second Turkic page has the Kyrgyz crushed in 709-710. Counterparts needing dossiers: xueyantuo (629-646, a steppe polity), second-turkic-khaganate (682-744). The Yenisei Kyrgyz page and the other pages are silent on Kyrgyz tribute in 587-630. Page budget: five pages, all cited. Reviewer fixes (second pass): (a) 630 gain of the Ordos from the Tang added and ledger 630 (Tang loss) written without the Ordos; (b) 639 loss and 642 gain of the Ordos outside the Hetao added, the 639 gain and the 642 loss reduced to the Hetao outside the Ordos (166 cells); all four against the Tang or the Xueyantuo as the pages allow. Cross-dossier convention: this dossier draws the Ashina settlement 630-645 as land of eastern-gokturks (taken from the Tang in the data); the Tang worked example carries it only as a vassal tint and its Cliopatria shape still holds the Ordos in 630-645, so ea-04 must remove the Ordos from the Tang's direct land for those years (or record the matching loss and gain). (c) The Ashina Simo page gives a seat for 641 only (Dingxiang), added to the capitals; the Second Turkic page links the Ordos Loop settlement to the 630 defeat but gives it no year.
